title: API Compatibility and Evolution
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of api compatibility and evolution in a FastAPI application.
Apply or interpret one example related to backward-compatible schema changes.
Identify one limitation or failure case and describe how to verify it.

content.intro: This lesson covers api compatibility and evolution within api design, versioning, and integration. Use the supplied syllabus topics as the coverage checklist, then connect them to the worked example and the verification task.
content.why_it_matters: You will use api compatibility and evolution to build APIs whose contracts and behavior are understandable to both clients and maintainers. The practical aim is predictable client-server contracts, resource naming, typed parameters and correct HTTP semantics.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: API Compatibility and Evolution matters because it is part of api design, versioning, and integration. In practice, focus on predictable client-server contracts, resource naming, typed parameters and correct HTTP semantics. A framework feature only helps when its assumptions match the application; keep input validation, business policy and side effects distinguishable.

items.title: Backward-compatible schema changes
items.text: For backward-compatible schema changes, define the accepted shape and constraints explicitly. Validate untrusted input at the boundary, distinguish omitted values from explicit nulls, and return only fields the caller is allowed to see.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Run: fastapi dev main.py; open http://127.0.0.1:8000/
content_blocks.reset_steps: For read-only examples, no reset is needed. For any example that writes state, use a disposable local database/test fixture; record the starting state and clean up only lab data. Never use production credentials or real personal data.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Adapt the example to cover “Backward-compatible schema changes”. Write down the expected success result and one invalid, missing, duplicate, timeout or permission-boundary case that matters for this topic.

task: Create a small reviewable artifact for “API Compatibility and Evolution”: explain its goal, cover the listed subtopics, show an example with expected result, then include one edge case and how you would verify it.
hints: Start with “Backward-compatible schema changes” and state the required inputs, output and assumptions.
Change one thing at a time; check the official reference and capture the actual response/error instead of guessing.
Include a negative/edge-case check and document which behavior remains untested.
expected_output: A reviewable example or design note for API Compatibility and Evolution, covering the PDF subtopics, expected behavior and at least one verification check.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a code fragment without checking its assumptions.
common_mistakes.why: Installed versions, imported types, application structure and external services affect behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: State assumptions; check the versioned official docs; run a minimal local test and add one failure case.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating one happy-path response as proof of correctness.
common_mistakes.why: Invalid input, permissions, concurrency, timeouts and cleanup are not exercised by a single request.
common_mistakes.fix: Add focused normal and negative tests and record exact expected status/body.

common_mistakes.why: Even short examples may mutate records, reveal data or affect availability.
common_mistakes.fix: Use synthetic inputs and a disposable environment; review security, cleanup and rollback before promotion.

summary: API Compatibility and Evolution belongs to the broader goal of predictable client-server contracts, resource naming, typed parameters and correct HTTP semantics.
Use the source subtopics as the completeness checklist and verify expected results rather than relying on intuition.
Examples in this course are illustrative until technically reviewed and executed on a supported local environment.
